assessments.reasoning: Five contiguous ranges cover the 73,482-byte SPDX json/details record, with reported SHA-256 9f8c6e6dc16cd05d9b9dc34ddd4a4e40df59f9813bae38d1f461ea245166fdf0. Part 1 gives isDeprecatedLicenseId=false. Part 3 gives licenseId=GPL-2.0-or-later and the standard header's “either version 2 of the License, or (at your option) any later version.” Its comment explicitly distinguishes GPL-2.0-only. The cited GNU standalone HTML, OSI and OpenJDK links supply leads with different authority and scope.

The official repository's annotated v3.29.0 tag targets commit 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48, which appears in all five retrievals of the or-later record. This verifies the release association. The tag is unsigned and carries no independent evidence about the notice's meaning.

The GNU publisher copy matches the claim's representation digest. Section 9 expressly permits the recipient to follow the specified version or any later FSF-published version when the program so specifies. The appendix supplies the corresponding example after “END OF TERMS AND CONDITIONS.” This establishes the meaning of the election in the notice.

challenge.method: Compared three cases against section 9 and both SPDX headers: a version-2-only notice, a version-2-or-later notice, and a notice specifying no version number. Also checked whether common source links or matching-template language selected an election.
challenge.results: Only the second case expressly gives the claimed version-2-or-later election. Section 9 separately permits any FSF-published version when the program specifies no number, which can include versions before 2. The common June 1991 heading and cited GNU and OpenJDK representations cannot resolve a particular file's notice.

limitations: The claim's “any later version” is bounded by section 9 to GPL versions published by the Foundation. The recipient may follow version 2. Exercising that choice does not turn the original notice into a version-2-only grant.

SPDX matching templates describe acceptable textual variation. A project's own notice determines its election and scope. The two generated entries establish license identifiers and provide no SPDX exception identifier, exception text, or exception-to-base mapping.
reasoning: SPDX License List 3.29.0 lists GPL-2.0-or-later for code whose applicable notice permits redistribution or modification under GPL version 2 or, at the recipient's option, any later GPL version published by the Free Software Foundation. The standard header states the election explicitly. Section 9 of the publisher text explains who may choose and which later versions qualify.
